t.bti: Ask about Bti for fixed water
t.drainPools: Map and drain shallow breeding pools
t.netCampaign: Distribute treated nets to top wards
t.clinicMalaria: Stock rapid tests and ACTs at clinics
t.lightTraps: Place light traps to confirm the signal
t.ovitraps: Place ovitraps to confirm the signal
t.sweepRain: Sweep rain-filled containers house to house
t.fixedWater: Treat water that cannot be removed
t.clinicDengue: Prepare clinics for a dengue rise
t.drainsRain: Treat storm drains after the rain
t.drains: Treat catch basins and storm drains
r.aedesWater: Eggs can stick to container walls above the waterline. Empty and scrub any containers you have; emptying water alone may leave eggs behind.
r.aedesWaterRain: Eggs can stick to container walls above the waterline; about {mm} mm of rain fell near {district} in the last 72 hours. Empty and scrub any containers you have; emptying water alone may leave eggs behind.
r.aedesDay: These mosquitoes can bite in daylight and at night. Use a locally registered skin repellent according to its label when outdoors.
r.culexWater: Floating egg rafts form on standing water. Check any drains or pools under your control and remove water where possible.
r.culexDusk: These mosquitoes are most active from dusk to dawn. Use a locally registered skin repellent according to its label when outdoors.
r.anophWater: Eggs may be laid near shallow water or marshy edges. If your property has shallow pools, drain them; leave public water treatment to health workers.
r.anophEvening: Many of these mosquitoes bite in the late evening or at night. Use a locally registered skin repellent according to its label when outdoors.
r.net: Many bite in the late evening or at night. In malaria-risk areas, an insecticide-treated net helps protect you while sleeping.
r.screens: Repair gaps and keep doors closed so mosquitoes cannot enter the home.
r.bti: If you have water that cannot be emptied or covered, Bti is a mosquito larvicide to ask a local health worker about. It does not kill biting adults. Check that a specific product is registered locally and its label allows that exact water site before use.
r.removeWaterRain: About {mm} mm of rain fell near {district} in the last 72 hours. Check containers, gutters, and pool covers; empty and scrub any that hold water.
r.removeWater: Check containers, gutters, and pool covers. Empty and scrub any water-holding items at least weekly.
r.repellent: Choose a locally registered skin repellent and follow its label, especially when spending time outdoors.
h.standRankDet: {district} ranks {rank} of {count} (risk {score}/100), with {detections} detections in the last 7 days.
h.standScoreDet: {district} has a risk score of {score}/100, with {detections} detections in the last 7 days.
h.rain: About {mm} mm of rain fell in the last 72 hours, so new breeding sites are likely.
h.fcFlatCases: Cases should hold near {w4} a week over the next 4 weeks (likely {low}–{high}).
h.fcRiseCases: Cases are forecast to rise from about {w1} to {w4} a week over the next 4 weeks (likely {low}–{high}).
h.fcFallCases: Cases are forecast to fall from about {w1} to {w4} a week over the next 4 weeks (likely {low}–{high}).
h.fcFlatPools: Positive mosquito pools should hold near {w4} a week over the next 4 weeks (likely {low}–{high}).
h.fcRisePools: Positive mosquito pools are forecast to rise from about {w1} to {w4} a week over the next 4 weeks (likely {low}–{high}).
h.fcFallPools: Positive mosquito pools are forecast to fall from about {w1} to {w4} a week over the next 4 weeks (likely {low}–{high}).
h.larval: Send teams to drain or fill shallow pools and puddles; larviciding is a supplement where sites are few, fixed and findable.
h.netCampaign: Insecticide-treated nets are the core malaria vector control tool. Prioritise households in {district} without a net or with nets older than about three years.
h.clinicMalaria: Ask clinics in {district} to test every fever and hold enough rapid tests and artemisinin-based treatment.
h.alertsMalaria: Reach households in {district} in local languages: sleep under a net every night and get tested within a day of any fever.
h.alertsDengue: Reach households in {district} in local languages: empty standing water weekly, use repellent during the day, and seek care for fever with severe pain.
h.alertsWnv: Reach households in {district} in local languages: use repellent from dusk to dawn, repair window screens, and empty water from containers.
h.lightTraps: Phone detections are opportunistic and skew toward phone owners. A few light traps in {district} confirm which mosquitoes are present before larger spending.
h.ovitraps: Phone detections are opportunistic and skew toward phone owners. A few ovitraps in {district} confirm which mosquitoes are present before larger spending.
h.sweep: Send field agents to empty, scrub or cover water tanks, buckets, tyres and plant pots, where most breeding happens.
h.fixedWaterBR: Where containers cannot be emptied or covered, field agents can apply a larvicide approved by the Ministry of Health. Use only registered products according to their label for that water site.
h.fixedWater: Where containers cannot be emptied or covered, field agents can apply a larvicide registered locally. Use only registered products according to their label for that water site.
h.clinicDengue: Brief clinics in {district} on warning signs and oral and IV fluids, and check test stock.
h.drains: Culex mosquitoes breed in catch basins and stagnant drains; treat them with a registered larvicide according to its label.
h.poolTesting: Trap and test more mosquito pools in {district} for West Nile virus to track how far it has spread.
h.clinician: Remind clinicians in {district} to test for West Nile virus in patients with fever, meningitis or encephalitis, and to report cases promptly.
h.adultControl: If positive pools keep rising, assess targeted adult mosquito control under your local plan and product labels.
